title: Samson's mother (Judges 13)
hookLine: the angel comes first to a woman whose name we never learn

cards: An angel of the Lord appears to a woman with no name. In the text she's the woman, his wife, Manoah's wife. She has no children.
And the angel comes not to her husband, but to her. You will conceive and bear a son, he says.

Drink no wine, eat nothing unclean, and no razor shall touch his head, for the child will be a Nazirite to God from the womb, and he will begin to save Israel from the Philistines. The hero of the next chapters is Samson.
But his story begins with her.

teach.b: She goes and tells her husband. Manoah prays: let the man of God come again, and teach us what to do.

teach.h: AGAIN TO HER, ALONE IN THE FIELD.
teach.b: The prayer is answered, and the angel comes again, but again to her, sitting alone in the field. Manoah isn't there; she has to run and fetch him.
When he asks for the rules for the child, the angel's answer mostly points back to her: of all that I said unto the woman, let her beware. Manoah offers a meal, then asks the angel's name.

teach.h: THE ANGEL WON'T GIVE HIS NAME.
teach.b: The angel won't give it: a name withheld, in a story about a woman whose name we never learn. Then Manoah lays an offering on a rock, the flame goes up toward heaven, and the angel goes up in the flame.
Manoah panics: we shall surely die, because we have seen God.

teach.h: SHE REASONS THEM OUT OF FEAR.
teach.b: And she reasons it through. "If the LORD were pleased to kill us, he would not have received a burnt offering and a meat offering at our hands." Nor would he have shown us all this, she says, or told us these things.
She's calm, and she's right. The text leaves her nameless; the Talmud gives her a name, Tzlelponit. Either way, the order of the story is plain.
The angel came to her, twice. She heard it first, and she was the one who understood it.

how: Jews read Judges 13 as the haftarah for the Torah portion Naso, which contains the laws of the Nazirite, and rabbinic tradition pays close attention to Manoah's wife and gives her a name.

o: the woman who betrayed Samson to the Philistines
a prophetess who judged Israel before Samson
the unnamed woman the angel visited first, twice

games.q: the angel came to her — tap the pairs.

s: the angel appeared to Manoah first
he came to Manoah's wife, and the second time came to her again, alone in the field.
Manoah's wife calmed him when he feared they would die
she reasoned: if God meant to kill us, he wouldn't have accepted our offering.
the book of Judges gives Samson's mother's name
it never does; the Talmud later gives her one.

games.q: you're Manoah's wife. the angel has just gone up in the flame, and your husband cries: we shall surely die, we have seen God. what do you say?
o: if God meant to kill us, he wouldn't have accepted our offering or told us all this.
games.why: she reasons him out of his fear: the offering was received, and the promise was given. she's calm, and she's right.

practice: Bring to mind someone whose name you never learned who did something for you anyway: the stranger who gave directions, the driver who waited while you ran for the bus, or someone in your family line whose name has been lost.
Hold them for a few breaths and thank them silently, without a name. If you pray, remember them in your own words.

wordCard.voice: Samson's mother. Never named in the text, visited by the angel first and twice, and the one who talked her husband out of his fear.

orig.note: Hebrew: Manoah's wife, the only name the book of Judges gives Samson's mother.

carryVoice: Your line: the angel came to her. The text kept her wisdom, if not her name. Day seven hundred twenty-three, done.
